newsitem.title: UK: Airline in probe after report wife flew jet.
newsitem.headline: Airline in probe after report wife flew jet.

text.p: A British airline said on Thursday it was investigating allegations that "operational procedures" had been breached after a newspaper claimed that one of its pilots had allowed his wife to fly a holiday jet.
But Britannia Airways said it could not confirm that the incident described in the tabloid Sun, which said a stewardess found the woman at the controls, actually occurred.
The Sun did not identify the pilot, or his co-pilot, who it said had also been suspended on full pay, or say where the flight was going to.
Britannia, Britain's largest charter airline specialising in holiday packages, said in a statement: "A full and thorough investigation is being carried out."
"Until this has been concluded the airline cannot and will not speculate on the nature, length or the outcome of the investigation," it added.
